Subject: SIG questionnaire initiation + SOC2/GDPR scope — quick recap & clarifying asks

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate you walking us through SustainHealth's integration goals and your timelines for vendor validation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Recap: SustainHealth will evaluate Redwood for patient-facing summarization features. You indicated PHI will be in-scope for a subset of workflows and that your legal team requires both HIPAA and GDPR controls documentation.
- Immediate ask: we'd like to kick off the SIG (or CAIQ if you prefer) prefill to minimize back-and-forth. I'm attaching a one-tab prefill template (SIG-prefill-template.xlsx) with suggested answers based on our conversation.
- Clarifying questions for your security/infosec & procurement teams (see below) — answers will let us scope evidence and estimate a delivery timeline.

Can you confirm the best contact for the procurement review (you mentioned procure@sustainhealth.com) and the security person who will own evidence collection? If you prefer a CAIQ instead of SIG, let me know — both are fine.

Clarifying questions (short):
1) SOC 2: do you require SOC 2 Type 2 or is Type 1 sufficient for initial evaluation? If Type 2, what measurement window (e.g., 6/12 months)?
2) Data residency: will any PHI need to be stored in a specific US region or do we only need to ensure no EU residency for this integration?
3) Subprocessors: do you require a full subprocessors list up front or is an attestation that subprocessors are audited acceptable?
4) Retention: expected retention period for logs and customer data (per workflow)?
5) KMS: do you require customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for exported data or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable with documented key rotation?

Next steps proposed:
- You confirm contacts and preferred questionnaire (SIG vs CAIQ)
- We return a prefilled SIG (attached) within 48 business hours for your review
- Schedule a quick 30-min sync with your security contact to walk the answers and evidence map

Attaching: SIG-prefill-template.xlsx + recording of today's demo.

Thanks — I'll loop Ben (solutions engineer) on any technical follow-ups.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
log.wright@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0124

Hi Logan — thanks for the detailed recap and for the template. A few quick answers and notes from our side: 

- Procurement contact: procure@sustainhealth.com (copied). They may route billing/contract questions separately.
- Security owner: Marcos Diaz (marcos.diaz@sustainhealth.com) will own evidence collection. I'll introduce him if needed.

Quick answers:
1) SOC 2: we require Type 2 for production vendors; 12-month window preferred.
2) Data residency: PHI must remain in US regions; we prefer east/central US but can accept other US regions with justification.
3) Subprocessors: procurement likes an upfront list, but a certified subprocessors attestation is often acceptable for early-stage evaluation — we'll confirm.
4) Retention: default retention request is 7 years for audit logs; for transient model inference logs 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
5) KMS: for PHI we prefer BYOK for exported data; internal processing can use vendor-managed KMS if keys are documented and rotate.

We'll need a brief evidence map before engaging legal. Please send the prefill and call invite once you have the primary security contact looped in.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product Ops, SustainHealth

Hi all — Kim from Redwood Security. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifying technical questions so the prefill is accurate: 

Confirmations: 
- SOC 2: Redwood has an in-scope SOC 2 Type 2 report (12-month window). We can share the redacted SOC 2 report and corresponding SOC 2 controls matrix for the requested period. Delivery: we can provide an initial redacted SOC 2 package with the prefill.
- KMS: Redwood supports both Redwood-managed KMS (default) and customer-managed BYOK for exported data; BYOK requires onboarding and a short key-exchange window.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessors registry and can provide either (a) a current CSV export of active subprocessors, or (b) a signed attestation statement. Happy to provide both.

Clarifying technical asks (so we scope evidence properly):
1) Exported PHI: please confirm which specific workflows will export PHI (e.g., summaries to EHR, SFTP export). This determines whether BYOK is mandatory for those flows.
2) Inference logs: when you say "audit logs 7 years," do you mean full inference payloads or metadata-only logs? We typically can retain metadata 7 years; full request/response payload retention beyond 90 days has platform and cost implications.
3) Regional endpoints: we will map regions to available deployment options (hosted vs. Dedicated vs. Private). If you need guaranteed east/central US hosting, we should discuss Dedicated or Private deployment lanes.

Next steps we will take once you confirm the two clarifying items:
- Return completed SIG prefill + evidence map (including SOC2 redacted package, subprocessors CSV) by Tue COB
- Schedule a 30-min technical security sync with Marcos to walk the evidence map and any timeline constraints

If procurement needs a BAA/DPA draft we can surface standard language for redlines; legal can follow after the evidence review.

Kim
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kim.park@redwoodinference.com
